cells.tense: What you want and the way forward are running level today, at one speed.
cells.act: move at the pace your feeling can sustain
cells.ask: Begin the piece you've been circling, its first stretch only, at a speed that could last a month rather than a day. The next step shows itself when you reach it.
cells.core:
You can want something and not need its whole shape settled first. What you're after gets felt through before it gets carried, and the two run level — enough light for the next step, the far end left fogged. That's why the plans of yours that hold actually hold; you're not forcing them past what the feeling can stand.

There's a stretch you've been circling. Begin it this week, the first part only, at a pace you could keep for a month and not for a single day. One turn holds the whole arc together, and the next one shows itself when you reach it. What's ahead stops reading as a wall the moment the first step is small enough to take.
cells.sheetLine: You don't need the far end to know the next step.
cells.place: out past where the road goes clear

cells.tense: You will have the next version before this one has had a chance to be finished.
cells.act: tend the resource with responsible care
cells.ask: Give something already underway seven days of the care it needs now, not the care its next version will ask for. Then look again at what grew.
cells.core:
Wanting is where you live, and right now it's a step ahead of everything else. What's here keeps turning into what's next before the present has been looked at, and people beside you feel the restlessness even while your hands stay steady on the work.

Take something already underway and tend it this week as the thing it is now, not the thing it's becoming. Care that doesn't exhaust and doesn't clutch is the whole of it, and seven days will show you which one you're doing. The future keeps its place at the edge of the room; it doesn't need to take the room. What's growing under your hand will answer either way, and both answers are useful.

cells.tense: You were at a door that mattered, and the standing here still has its shape.
cells.act: hold two true things without declaring either
cells.ask: Carry both sides of something you see clearly for several days without saying which side wins. Keep the page open; a few quiet days is the whole ask.
cells.core:
What used to move has gone quiet, and the next step is harder to find than it should be. Somewhere in you learned to stand at the far end of a decision, and today still carries that posture. Not gone. Not through.

Holding something true without announcing it is a skill you've used before, in quieter rooms. Take up two sides of something you see clearly, both in view, and keep them with you a few days — no declaration, no landing. What comes back comes back the way it went: something carried long enough to be trusted, and the next step is there when you look.
cells.sheetLine: The next step comes through something held, not something said.

cells.tense: The hand that's been shaping this is yours, and you're still counting it as weather.
cells.act: strike one thing from the list that does not serve
cells.ask: Cut a line from a list you're carrying — the one that doesn't serve what you're after. Leave it struck where you'll see it for a few days.
cells.core:
You've been moving through uncertainty without forcing it, and the account says the way opened, or the timing was off, or circumstances did it. The navigating is happening. The name on it is not.

Not-signing can spread into what you carry: what you keep, what you set down. Take a list, a schedule, a standing habit, and cut the line that doesn't serve what you're after. One line. Keep it where you'll see it a few days with that line gone. Sorting what matters from what doesn't is the skill you've been using; marking the cut as yours is the smaller step.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is the mechanism-first phrasing in the Too Much core: 'vision is multiplying past what's been felt' implies the record says the capacity is over-producing, which it doesn't; the record says the capacity is present and the seat is fine. Better to read the mechanism from what the person does — waiting for the sky to clear, keeping the next thing possible — which the record does support. The reader could reasonably object that 'always about to' is sharper than the evidence and that the Too Little core locates them at a closed door in a way they may not recognize. The ask survives being wrong in every cell: the tiny stewardship act remains useful even if the diagnosis is off, provided the ask is not tied to a feeling-state. The sentence that serves the writer more than the person is the Too Much handle 'the clear sky is what you're waiting for' — cut it. For Unacknowledged, drop 'moves everything with it' — it overclaims the size of the effect. Write the asks as stated, keep them under forty words, no safe person required.
